Section 1.  Subordination.

This Lease shall be subordinate to the lien of any present or future mortgage upon the Leased Premises only if, and to the extent that, the holder of such mortgage first enters into a written subordination, non-disturbance, and attornment agreement with Tenant, in form reasonably acceptable to Tenant and in recordable form, providing that so long as Tenant is not in default beyond any applicable cure period, Tenant’s possession of the Leased Premises and its rights under this Lease, including this Article X, shall not be disturbed by reason of any foreclosure or other enforcement action. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain such an agreement from its current mortgage holder, if any, within sixty (60) days after the Effective Date.

This Lease shall be subordinate to all present and future mortgages, and Tenant shall attorn to any successor owner. Upon request, Tenant shall execute an SNDA within ten (10) business days on the lender’s then-current commercially reasonable form, providing customary non-disturbance protection so long as no Event of Default exists. Landlord shall use commercially reasonable efforts to request an SNDA from its current lender, but shall not be liable if the lender declines or conditions delivery. Tenant shall provide each lender written notice of any Landlord default and a reasonable opportunity to cure before exercising any offset, self-help, or termination right.

Section 3.  Additional Rent; Operating Expenses.  In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay as additional rent (“Additional Rent”) Tenant’s proportionate share (based on the square footage of the Leased Premises relative to the total leasable square footage of the building) of Landlord’s

reasonable, actual, and customary costs of: (a) real estate taxes and assessments in accordance with Article VI; (b) commercially reasonable insurance premiums for the insurance Landlord is required to maintain under Article XII; and (c) reasonable costs of operating, maintaining, and repairing common areas serving the building, including shared parking areas (collectively

reasonable costs of owning, operating, maintaining, repairing, replacing, managing, and insuring the building and common areas, including real estate taxes and assessments; insurance premiums; utilities; security; refuse and snow removal; common-area maintenance and repair; and a management fee equal to three percent (3%) of gross rents (collectively
, “Operating Expenses”).

Operating Expenses shall exclude, in all cases, capital expenditures, reserves, depreciation, debt service, leasing commissions, and costs of a capital nature except as expressly permitted under Article VIII. Landlord shall provide Tenant with an annual estimate of Additional Rent, payable in equal monthly installments, together with an annual reconciliation against actual, invoiced costs within ninety (90) days after the end of each calendar year, accompanied by reasonably detailed supporting documentation, and Tenant shall have the right to audit Landlord’s books and records relating to Operating Expenses upon reasonable prior notice, at Tenant’s expense unless such audit reveals an overstatement of Operating Expenses in excess of three percent (3%), in which case Landlord shall bear the reasonable cost of the audit and promptly refund the overstated amount.

Operating Expenses shall also include capital expenditures required by laws enacted after the date of this Lease or reasonably intended to reduce Operating Expenses, in each case amortized over the item’s useful life with interest at the rate reasonably charged by Landlord’s lender. Costs attributable solely to Tenant’s clinical operations, including regulated medical waste, supplemental security or janitorial service, and after-hours HVAC, shall be billed directly to Tenant and shall not be subject to the cap in Section 4. Landlord shall provide an annual estimate and reconciliation with reasonably detailed supporting documentation. Tenant may audit Operating Expenses once per calendar year, at Tenant’s cost, by a qualified auditor not compensated on a contingency basis, upon written notice given within ninety (90) days after receipt of the reconciliation; Landlord shall reimburse reasonable audit costs only if the audit establishes an overstatement exceeding five percent (5%).
